report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/content shift — Model B (B − A positive) pushes generation toward food/cooking/restaurant/baking tokens compared with Model A.

Why I conclude this
- The L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in late layers (layers ~16–25), especially at early token positions, which is where residual differences tend to affect final token selection.
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking/food/restaurant vocabulary across many late-layer, early-position cells: e.g. "restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Chef", "kitchen", "Kitchen", "Cook", "Cooked", "hot", "microwave", "baked", "Chef", "Cheesecake", etc. These tokens recur across layers 16–25 and positions 1–4.
- Earlier-layer signals (smaller magnitude) include suffix-like fragments ("ist", "oot") and some niche tokens ("chiropractic", "cadmium", "dissertation", "billionaire", "metropolitan") but the dominant, high-magnitude signature in the layers that matter for output is the culinary/restaurant cluster.

Caveats
- I cannot identify a more specific training objective or intent (e.g., "promote recipes" vs "demote non-food topics") from this evidence alone. The safe interpretation is that B increases probability mass on food/restaurant/cooking-related continuations relative to A.
